en: The Jātaka:
The Section of Eleven, Chapter on the Supporter of His Mother.
8. The Saṃvara Jātaka “O Great King,
the lord of men knows your virtue;”
By honoring these princes,
do not think that you have honored anyone else.
While our two great kings remain, [they are the ones to be honored].
When the King had passed away,
his kinsmen gave their consent,
seeing it as beneficial for themselves.
By what restraint do you stand firm when [defilements] have arisen?
By what do they not overcome you?
“The assembly of kinsmen has gathered together.
“I bear no ill will, O Prince,
toward the great seers, the ascetics.”
I pay you full homage; I revere the feet of you, the Tādin.
May they [establish] me, who am devoted to the qualities of the Dhamma, [in those same qualities].
The seers, who delight in the qualities of the Dhamma, instruct the ascetic who is willing to listen and free from envy.
Having heard the words of those great seers, the ascetics,
I did not hold anything in contempt.
My mind is devoted to the Dhamma.
There are elephant riders, those who serve in the army,
charioteers, and infantrymen.
I do not withhold from them their established food and wages;
and I have ministers for them.
The ministers were attendants who conducted trade in Benares,
dealing in much meat and strong liquor.
Moreover, there were prosperous merchants who had come from various countries;
among them, protection was established by me.
“Know this to be the Uposatha.
“O Saṃvara, rule the kingdom of your kinsmen in accordance with the Dhamma.”
You were wise and learned,
and also a benefactor to your kinsmen;
surrounded by those very kinsmen, [you have passed away].
Adorned with various jewels,
enemies cannot overcome him,
just as the lord of the asuras could not overcome Indra.
The Saṃvara Jātaka, the eighth.
